---
title: "Project files"
---

ACE projects are saved as `.ace` files.

## What a project file contains

A project file stores imported source text, codebook entries, annotations, notes, coder information, and related project data.

The file is local to your machine unless you deliberately move, copy, sync, or share it.

## Backups

Treat `.ace` files as research data. Keep backups and avoid editing them manually.

## Opening projects from other ACE versions

ACE updates projects made by older versions automatically the first time it opens them, and saves the update into the file.

A project made by a newer version of ACE is not opened: ACE tells you to update ACE first and leaves the file unchanged.

## Copying and syncing projects

Close the project, or quit ACE, before you copy, move, back up, or sync an `.ace` file.

While a project is open, ACE may keep temporary journal files beside it, named like the project (for example `Interviews.ace-wal` and `Interviews.ace-shm`). Recent work can sit in those files, so a copy taken while ACE is open may be incomplete. ACE folds them into the `.ace` file when you close the project or quit normally. Do not delete them; if ACE closes unexpectedly, it recovers from them the next time the project is opened.

After a clean close, the single `.ace` file is all you need.

## Privacy

ACE does not require a cloud account and does not upload project files automatically. If you store `.ace` files in a cloud-synced folder, that sync is controlled by your storage provider, not by ACE.
